questionText: Organizational behaviour (OB) is best defined as:
options: The study of financial performance and accounting practices within organizations
The systematic study of how individuals, groups, and structures affect and are affected by behaviour within organizations
The management of physical resources and production systems in organizations
The study of marketing strategies used by organizations to attract customers

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the primary goal of studying organizational behaviour?
options: To maximize the financial returns of shareholders through efficient management
To improve organizational effectiveness by understanding and influencing human behaviour at work
To design optimal production processes that minimize waste and cost
To develop legal frameworks governing employment relationships

questionText: Which of the following disciplines has contributed MOST significantly to the study of organizational behaviour?
options: Engineering, physics, and chemistry
Psychology, sociology, anthropology, and political science
Accounting, finance, and economics only
Marketing, logistics, and supply chain management

questionText: The contribution of "psychology" to organizational behaviour is MOST evident in the study of:
options: Organizational culture across different national contexts
Group dynamics and intergroup conflict in organizations
Individual behaviour, attitudes, perception, motivation, and learning
The distribution of power and authority in organizational structures

questionText: "Sociology" contributes to organizational behaviour primarily through its focus on:
options: Individual cognitive processes such as perception and decision-making
Group behaviour, organizational culture, formal structures, and intergroup dynamics
The psychological foundations of individual motivation and personality
The application of mathematical models to organizational decision-making

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the "systems perspective" in organizational behaviour?
options: Organizations are viewed as collections of independent individuals whose behaviours do not affect each other
Organizations are viewed as interconnected systems where individual, group, and organizational factors continuously interact
Organizational behaviour is determined exclusively by the formal authority structure
Individual behaviour in organizations is driven solely by financial incentives

questionText: Which of the following is a key dependent variable traditionally studied in organizational behaviour?
options: Return on investment and earnings per share
Employee productivity, job satisfaction, absenteeism, and turnover
Market share and competitive positioning
Supplier performance and procurement lead times

questionText: "Organizational effectiveness" in the context of OB refers to:
options: The degree to which an organization maximizes its use of physical resources
The degree to which an organization achieves its goals while maintaining employee satisfaction and well-being
The financial profitability of the organization relative to its competitors
The compliance of the organization with all relevant legal and regulatory requirements

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the relationship between individual behaviour and organizational outcomes in OB?
options: Individual behaviour has no significant impact on organizational performance
Individual behaviour, shaped by personal characteristics and the work environment, directly influences group and organizational performance
Organizational outcomes are determined exclusively by structural and strategic factors, not human behaviour
Individual behaviour only matters at the senior management level, not among front-line employees

questionText: The "contingency approach" in organizational behaviour suggests that:
options: There is one universally effective way to manage people in all organizational situations
The most effective management approach depends on the specific situation, individuals involved, and organizational context
Employee behaviour is entirely determined by organizational structure and formal rules
Financial incentives are the most effective motivators in all organizational contexts

questionText: Which of the following correctly describes the "behavioural science approach" to studying organizations?
options: It relies exclusively on philosophical reasoning and managerial experience
It applies scientific research methods to study human behaviour in organizations to generate reliable, generalizable knowledge
It focuses solely on financial performance indicators to evaluate organizational effectiveness
It uses engineering principles to optimize production systems and work processes

questionText: Organizational behaviour research uses which of the following methods to study workplace behaviour?
options: Financial auditing and budget variance analysis
Surveys, field studies, laboratory experiments, and case studies
Engineering time-and-motion studies exclusively
Marketing focus groups and customer satisfaction surveys

questionText: Which of the following is an example of an "organizational-level" variable in OB?
options: An individual employee's personality traits and cognitive abilities
The dynamics and cohesion of a work team
The organization's culture, structure, and human resource policies
The interpersonal relationship between two colleagues

questionText: "Job satisfaction" in organizational behaviour is BEST defined as:
options: The degree to which an employee earns compensation above the industry average
The positive emotional state resulting from an individual's appraisal of their job and job experiences
The extent to which an employee complies with organizational rules and procedures
The level of physical comfort provided by the employee's work environment

questionText: Which of the following statements about organizational behaviour is TRUE?
options: OB focuses exclusively on individual behaviour and ignores group and organizational factors
OB is a purely theoretical field with no practical applications in management
OB draws on multiple disciplines to provide a comprehensive understanding of human behaviour in work settings
OB is only relevant to human resources departments and has no value for operations or logistics managers

questionText: Which of the following personal characteristics MOST directly influences individual behaviour in organizations?
options: The employee's geographic location and commute distance
Personality, values, attitudes, perception, and abilities
The employee's physical appearance and dress code compliance
The number of years the employee has worked in the same office location

questionText: "Personality" in organizational behaviour is BEST defined as:
options: The physical appearance and social status of an individual
The stable pattern of behaviours, thoughts, and emotions that characterizes an individual and distinguishes them from others
The set of technical skills and competencies an individual brings to the workplace
The level of education and professional qualifications attained by an individual

questionText: The "Big Five" personality model identifies which of the following dimensions?
options: Intelligence, creativity, ambition, resilience, and empathy
Openness to experience, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism
Motivation, attitude, perception, learning, and values
Leadership, teamwork, communication, problem-solving, and adaptability

questionText: Which Big Five personality trait is MOST strongly associated with high job performance across a wide range of occupations?
options: Extraversion
Agreeableness
Conscientiousness
Openness to experience

questionText: "Locus of control" as a personality dimension refers to:
options: The degree to which an individual prefers structured versus unstructured work environments
The extent to which individuals believe they control the events that affect their lives versus attributing outcomes to external forces
The level of emotional stability an individual demonstrates under work pressure
The degree to which an individual seeks social interaction and external stimulation

questionText: An employee with a high "internal locus of control" is MOST likely to:
options: Attribute their success or failure to luck and external circumstances
Believe that their own efforts and abilities determine their outcomes and take responsibility for results
Rely heavily on their supervisor for direction and decision-making
Avoid challenging tasks to minimize the risk of failure

questionText: "Self-efficacy" in organizational behaviour refers to:
options: The degree to which an individual values financial compensation above other work rewards
An individual's belief in their own ability to successfully perform a specific task or achieve a goal
The tendency of individuals to evaluate themselves more favorably than their peers
The level of social intelligence an individual demonstrates in group settings

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes "attitude" in the context of organizational behaviour?
options: A stable personality trait that determines how an individual responds to all situations
A learned predisposition to respond in a consistently favourable or unfavourable manner toward a given object, person, or situation
The set of technical skills and competencies an employee applies in their job
The formal evaluation of an employee's performance by their direct supervisor

questionText: The three components of an attitude are:
options: Motivation, ability, and opportunity
Cognitive, affective, and behavioural components
Input, process, and output components
Strategic, tactical, and operational components

questionText: "Cognitive dissonance" in organizational behaviour occurs when:
options: An employee experiences a gap between their current skill level and job requirements
An individual holds two or more conflicting attitudes or beliefs simultaneously, creating psychological discomfort
A team is unable to reach consensus on a decision due to conflicting opinions
An organization's goals conflict with the personal values of its employees

questionText: "Organizational commitment" refers to:
options: The formal employment contract between an employee and the organization
The degree to which an employee identifies with and is emotionally attached to the organization and its goals
The financial investment an employee has made in the organization through stock ownership
The legal obligation of an employee to fulfill the terms of their employment agreement

questionText: "Perception" in organizational behaviour is BEST defined as:
options: The objective measurement of external stimuli by an individual's sensory system
The process by which individuals select, organize, and interpret sensory information to give meaning to their environment
The formal evaluation of organizational performance against set targets
The mathematical calculation of probability and expected outcomes in decision-making

questionText: The "halo effect" in perception refers to:
options: The tendency to attribute the behaviour of others to situational factors rather than personal characteristics
The tendency to draw a general impression of a person based on a single prominent characteristic
The tendency to perceive one's own group as superior to other groups
The tendency to evaluate others more favorably when they are physically attractive

questionText: "Stereotyping" in organizational behaviour refers to:
options: Evaluating an individual based on a direct observation of their actual behaviour
Judging an individual based on generalizations about the group to which they belong
The tendency to perceive recent events as more significant than earlier events
Forming impressions of others based exclusively on their professional qualifications

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the "fundamental attribution error" in organizational behaviour?
options: The tendency to attribute one's own failures to situational factors while crediting personal ability for successes
The tendency to overestimate the influence of personal dispositions and underestimate situational factors when explaining others' behaviour
The tendency to perceive group members as more similar to each other than they actually are
The tendency to evaluate others based on the most recently observed behaviour

questionText: "Learning" in organizational behaviour is BEST defined as:
options: A temporary change in behaviour caused by fatigue or physical injury
A relatively permanent change in behaviour or knowledge that results from experience or practice
The acquisition of formal academic qualifications through university education
The memorization of organizational rules and procedures during employee orientation

questionText: "Classical conditioning" as a learning theory was pioneered by:
options: B.F. Skinner
Albert Bandura
Ivan Pavlov
Abraham Maslow

questionText: "Operant conditioning" in organizational behaviour suggests that behaviour is shaped by:
options: The unconscious drives and instincts of the individual
The consequences that follow behaviour — reinforcement increases behaviour, punishment decreases it
The social observation and imitation of role models in the work environment
The cognitive reasoning and conscious decision-making of the individual

questionText: Which of the following is an example of "positive reinforcement" in the workplace?
options: Suspending an employee without pay for repeated tardiness
Removing an unpleasant task from an employee's workload when they meet performance targets
Awarding a bonus to an employee who consistently exceeds their sales targets
Issuing a formal written warning to an employee for a policy violation

questionText: "Negative reinforcement" in operant conditioning refers to:
options: Punishing undesirable behaviour by applying an unpleasant consequence
Strengthening a behaviour by removing an unpleasant stimulus when the desired behaviour occurs
Ignoring undesirable behaviour until it is extinguished
Reducing a desired behaviour by applying an unpleasant consequence

questionText: "Social learning theory," proposed by Albert Bandura, emphasizes that learning occurs through:
options: The systematic application of rewards and punishments by managers
Observation and imitation of others, combined with self-regulation and cognitive processes
The classical conditioning of automatic responses to environmental stimuli
The formal instruction provided by trainers in classroom settings

questionText: "Self-reinforcement" as a concept in social learning theory refers to:
options: Receiving praise and recognition from a supervisor for good performance
Individuals regulating their own behaviour by setting internal standards and rewarding themselves when those standards are met
The automatic repetition of behaviour patterns without conscious awareness
The process of learning new skills through structured mentoring programs

questionText: Which of the following reinforcement schedules produces the MOST resistant-to-extinction behaviour?
options: Continuous reinforcement schedule
Fixed-ratio reinforcement schedule
Fixed-interval reinforcement schedule
Variable-ratio reinforcement schedule

questionText: "Organizational behaviour modification" (OB Mod) applies which learning principle to improve employee performance?
options: Social learning theory through role modelling and mentoring programs
Classical conditioning through stimulus-response pairing in the workplace
Operant conditioning principles — systematically reinforcing desirable behaviours and extinguishing undesirable ones
Cognitive learning theory through structured training and development programs

questionText: "Values" in organizational behaviour are BEST described as:
options: The specific skills and technical competencies an employee brings to the job
Basic convictions about what is right, good, or desirable that guide individual behaviour and judgment
The formal performance standards set by management for each employee
The financial compensation and benefits package provided to employees

questionText: A "group" in organizational behaviour is BEST defined as:
options: Any collection of people who happen to be in the same physical location
Two or more individuals who interact, are interdependent, and come together to achieve particular objectives
A formally designated organizational unit with a defined reporting structure
A permanent committee established by senior management to oversee a specific function

questionText: Which of the following BEST distinguishes a "team" from a "group" in organizational behaviour?
options: Teams are larger than groups and include more members
Teams have synergistic performance, shared accountability, and complementary skills; groups may simply share information
Groups are always formally designated by management; teams are always informal
Teams are temporary; groups are permanent fixtures of the organizational structure

questionText: "Formal groups" in organizations are BEST described as:
options: Groups that emerge spontaneously based on friendship and shared interests
Groups defined by the organization's structure with designated work assignments and established relationships
Groups formed by employees without management involvement or approval
Groups that operate outside the formal organizational hierarchy

questionText: "Informal groups" in organizations typically form due to:
options: Formal management directives assigning employees to specific project teams
Common interests, friendships, social proximity, or shared values among employees
Organizational restructuring that creates new reporting relationships
The need to comply with regulatory requirements for employee consultation

questionText: Tuckman's model of group development identifies which of the following stages in sequence?
options: Forming, performing, storming, norming, adjourning
Storming, forming, norming, performing, adjourning
Forming, storming, norming, performing, adjourning
Norming, forming, storming, performing, adjourning

questionText: During the "storming" stage of group development, which of the following is MOST likely to occur?
options: Group members are polite and cautious, getting to know one another
Intragroup conflict emerges as members resist constraints and assert their individuality
The group develops cohesion and establishes strong norms and working relationships
The group focuses intensely on task completion with high levels of performance

questionText: "Group norms" in organizational behaviour are BEST described as:
options: The formal performance standards set by management for each team
Acceptable standards of behaviour shared by group members that define what members should and should not do
The written rules documented in the organization's employee handbook
The individual behavioural tendencies each member brings to the group

questionText: "Group cohesiveness" refers to:
options: The degree to which group members have complementary technical skills
The degree to which group members are attracted to each other and motivated to remain in the group
The level of agreement among group members on the tasks to be performed
The formal authority structure governing interactions among group members

questionText: Which of the following is a potential NEGATIVE consequence of high group cohesiveness combined with low performance norms?
options: Excessive competition among group members for leadership positions
High productivity driven by strong interpersonal relationships
Strong social bonds that support individual performance regardless of group norms
Low productivity as the cohesive group enforces norms of restricting output

questionText: "Social loafing" in group behaviour refers to:
options: The tendency of individuals to work harder when in a group than when alone
The tendency of individuals to exert less effort when working in a group than when working alone
The conflict that arises when group members disagree about task assignments
The tendency of groups to make riskier decisions than individuals

questionText: Which of the following strategies is MOST effective for reducing social loafing in work groups?
options: Increasing the size of the group to distribute responsibility more broadly
Making individual contributions identifiable and holding each member accountable for specific outcomes
Eliminating all performance standards so members feel less pressured
Reducing the importance and visibility of the group's task

questionText: "Groupthink" in organizational behaviour occurs when:
options: Group members engage in vigorous debate to arrive at the best possible decision
The desire for conformity and harmony in a cohesive group overrides realistic appraisal of alternatives, leading to poor decisions
Diverse perspectives within a group create conflict that prevents decision-making
Group members defer all major decisions to the most senior or expert member

questionText: Which of the following is a symptom of "groupthink"?
options: Encouragement of diverse opinions and devil's advocacy within the group
Rigorous critical evaluation of all proposed alternatives before a decision is made
The illusion of invulnerability and collective rationalization of contrary evidence
Assignment of a formal devil's advocate to challenge all group decisions

questionText: "Group polarization" in decision-making refers to:
options: The tendency of groups to reach a compromise position between extreme individual views
The tendency of groups to make more extreme decisions than the average initial position of individual members
The tendency of groups to avoid making decisions due to excessive conflict
The tendency of groups to defer to the most senior member's initial position

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the concept of "role" in a group context?
options: The formal job title assigned to an individual by the organization
A set of expected behaviour patterns attributed to someone occupying a given position in a group
The level of authority delegated to an individual within the group hierarchy
The financial compensation associated with an individual's position in the organization

questionText: "Role conflict" in organizational behaviour occurs when:
options: An individual is assigned too many tasks to complete within the available time
An individual faces incompatible expectations from different role senders or role requirements
Two group members compete for the same leadership position within a team
A group member lacks the technical skills required to fulfill their assigned role

questionText: "Role ambiguity" in organizational behaviour refers to:
options: Conflict between the demands of two different roles held simultaneously by an individual
Uncertainty about what behaviours are expected of a person in a given role
The tendency of individuals to take on more roles than they can effectively fulfill
Disagreement among group members about who should lead the team

questionText: "Status" in group dynamics refers to:
options: The formal rank assigned to a position in the organizational hierarchy
A socially defined position or rank given to groups or group members by others, reflecting their perceived prestige
The level of technical expertise demonstrated by a group member
The financial compensation and benefits associated with an employee's position

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the concept of "intergroup conflict" in organizations?
options: Disagreements between individual employees about task assignments
Conflict that arises between different groups or departments within an organization
Conflict that occurs within a single team due to personality differences
Disagreements between managers and subordinates about performance standards

questionText: Which of the following is the MOST effective approach for managing and resolving intergroup conflict?
options: Ignoring the conflict and hoping it resolves itself over time
Separating the conflicting groups by eliminating all interaction between them
Identifying superordinate goals that both groups share and encouraging collaborative problem-solving
Replacing the leaders of both groups with new managers from outside

questionText: "Motivation" in organizational behaviour is BEST defined as:
options: The financial compensation provided to employees in exchange for their work
The processes that account for an individual's intensity, direction, and persistence of effort toward achieving a goal
The formal performance management system used to evaluate employee productivity
The set of rules and procedures that govern employee behaviour in the organization

questionText: Maslow's hierarchy of needs theory arranges human needs in which of the following orders from LOWEST to HIGHEST?
options: Social, physiological, safety, esteem, self-actualization
Self-actualization, esteem, social, safety, physiological
Physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-actualization
Safety, physiological, social, esteem, self-actualization

questionText: According to Maslow's theory, which of the following workplace conditions addresses "safety needs"?
options: Providing opportunities for promotion and career advancement
Organizing company social events and team-building activities
Offering job security, safe working conditions, and health benefits
Recognizing outstanding employee contributions publicly

questionText: Alderfer's ERG theory modifies Maslow's model by proposing which of the following need categories?
options: Existence, relatedness, and growth needs
Physiological, safety, and social needs
Achievement, power, and affiliation needs
Hygiene, motivator, and growth needs

questionText: A key difference between Alderfer's ERG theory and Maslow's hierarchy is that ERG theory:
options: Proposes a strict hierarchical progression through needs levels with no regression
Allows for simultaneous pursuit of multiple need levels and includes a frustration-regression principle
Identifies only two categories of needs rather than five
Focuses exclusively on the needs of managers rather than all employees

questionText: According to Herzberg's two-factor theory, which of the following is a "hygiene factor"?
options: Achievement and recognition
The nature and content of the work itself
Opportunities for advancement and personal growth
Company policy, supervision quality, and working conditions

questionText: Herzberg's theory implies that to truly MOTIVATE employees, managers should focus on:
options: Improving physical working conditions and increasing base salaries
Ensuring job security and providing adequate employee benefits
Enriching jobs with more responsibility, recognition, achievement, and growth opportunities
Strengthening organizational policies and improving supervisory practices

questionText: McClelland's need for "achievement" (nAch) is BEST characterized by a preference for:
options: Controlling and influencing the behaviour of other people
Maintaining warm, close relationships and social acceptance
Moderately challenging tasks with clear feedback and personal responsibility for outcomes
Highly routine tasks that offer consistent and predictable results

questionText: McClelland's need for "power" (nPow) refers to the desire to:
options: Accomplish challenging tasks and receive recognition for personal achievement
Influence, control, and have an impact on the behaviour of others
Build and maintain close, cooperative relationships with colleagues
Achieve progressively higher levels of personal and professional growth

questionText: McClelland's need for "affiliation" (nAff) is MOST evident in employees who:
options: Seek positions of authority and control over others
Prefer competitive, high-stakes tasks with significant performance pressure
Prioritize social relationships, teamwork, and being liked by colleagues over task achievement
Focus intensely on personal achievement and prefer to work independently

questionText: Vroom's expectancy theory proposes that motivation is a function of which three variables?
options: Needs, goals, and rewards
Expectancy, instrumentality, and valence
Reinforcement, punishment, and extinction
Equity, fairness, and social comparison

questionText: "Expectancy" in Vroom's theory refers to:
options: The perceived value or attractiveness of the outcome to the individual
The belief that a given level of performance will lead to a desired outcome or reward
The belief that effort will result in the desired level of performance
The fairness of the relationship between inputs and outcomes

questionText: "Instrumentality" in Vroom's expectancy theory refers to:
options: The individual's belief that increased effort will lead to higher performance
The degree to which the individual values the reward being offered
The individual's belief that achieving a certain performance level will lead to a desired reward
The comparison of one's own input-outcome ratio with that of a reference person

questionText: "Valence" in Vroom's expectancy theory refers to:
options: The belief that effort will lead to the desired performance level
The belief that performance will lead to a specific outcome
The value or attractiveness the individual places on a particular outcome or reward
The perception of fairness in the distribution of rewards in the organization

questionText: Adams' equity theory predicts that employees who perceive they are being UNDER-rewarded relative to a comparison person will MOST likely:
options: Increase their inputs to justify the higher reward they feel they deserve
Reduce their effort, increase their outcomes through other means, or distort their perception to restore equity
Accept the inequity and continue performing at the same level
Request additional responsibilities to demonstrate their value to the organization

questionText: Goal-setting theory, proposed by Locke and Latham, suggests that motivation and performance are HIGHEST when goals are:
options: Vague and open-ended to allow employee creativity and flexibility
Set exclusively by management without employee involvement
Specific, challenging, and accompanied by feedback
Easy to achieve to build employee confidence and self-efficacy

questionText: Which of the following correctly describes the application of goal-setting theory in a logistics firm?
options: Allowing employees to set their own highly personal goals with no connection to organizational targets
Setting specific delivery performance targets, communicating them clearly, providing regular feedback, and involving employees in the goal-setting process
Setting goals so challenging that they are rarely achievable to maximize employee effort
Avoiding formal goal-setting to preserve employee autonomy and creativity

questionText: "Job enrichment" as a motivational strategy involves:
options: Adding more tasks of the same difficulty and complexity to an employee's job
Increasing the pay and financial benefits associated with an employee's position
Redesigning jobs to include greater responsibility, autonomy, skill variety, and opportunities for growth
Assigning employees to work in different departments on a rotating basis

questionText: Hackman and Oldham's "Job Characteristics Model" identifies which of the following as a core job dimension that influences motivation?
options: Compensation level, working hours, and physical work environment
Skill variety, task identity, task significance, autonomy, and feedback
Organizational culture, management style, and peer relationships
Job security, promotion opportunities, and training availability

questionText: According to the Job Characteristics Model, "task identity" refers to:
options: The degree to which the job has a substantial impact on the lives of others
The degree to which the job requires a variety of different activities and skills
The degree to which the job involves completing a whole and identifiable piece of work from beginning to end
The degree to which the job provides direct and clear information about performance effectiveness

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes "intrinsic rewards" in the context of work motivation?
options: Salary increases, bonuses, and promotions provided by the organization
Personal satisfaction, sense of achievement, and pride derived from the work itself
Recognition awards and certificates presented at annual company events
Additional paid leave and flexible working arrangements offered by the employer

questionText: "Extrinsic rewards" in motivation refer to:
options: The personal satisfaction and fulfilment an employee derives from doing meaningful work
Tangible rewards such as pay, benefits, promotions, and recognition provided by the organization
The intrinsic pleasure an employee experiences from mastering a challenging task
The emotional support and encouragement provided by a supervisor or mentor

questionText: Which of the following is the MOST direct application of motivation theory in a logistics and supply chain context?
options: Using financial penalties to discourage all forms of employee error or delay
Designing jobs with clear performance targets, providing regular feedback, recognizing achievement, and creating opportunities for growth
Standardizing all job roles to maximize predictability and operational efficiency
Eliminating all forms of employee discretion to ensure consistent operational execution

questionText: A logistics manager notices that experienced warehouse employees are disengaged despite receiving competitive salaries. Applying Herzberg's theory, which action is MOST likely to re-engage them?
options: Further increasing their base salaries and adding overtime bonuses
Improving the physical working conditions of the warehouse
Enriching their jobs by delegating more decision-making authority and providing challenging assignments
Reducing supervision to give them more freedom in how they perform their routine tasks

questionText: Which of the following BEST explains why motivation theories are important for managers in supply chain organizations?
options: Motivation theories provide legal frameworks for managing employment contracts
Understanding motivation enables managers to design work environments and incentive systems that enhance employee performance, commitment, and retention
Motivation theories eliminate the need for formal performance management systems
Motivation theory applies only to senior managers, not to front-line logistics workers

questionText: "Power" in organizational behaviour is BEST defined as:
options: The formal authority granted to a manager by the organization's hierarchy
The capacity to influence the behaviour of others to act in accordance with one's wishes
The financial resources available to a manager to reward or punish subordinates
The legal right of senior management to make binding decisions for the organization

questionText: French and Raven identified five bases of social power. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
options: Reward power
Coercive power
Financial power
Referent power

questionText: "Legitimate power" in an organization derives from:
options: The personal qualities and charisma of the power holder
The ability to control valued resources and provide desired rewards
The formal position held by the individual in the organizational hierarchy
The special knowledge and expertise possessed by the individual

questionText: "Reward power" in organizational behaviour refers to the ability to:
options: Threaten and apply punishment for non-compliance with directives
Influence others through the distribution of valued positive outcomes such as pay, promotions, and recognition
Influence others through personal charm and the desire to be associated with the power holder
Influence others through access to and control of important organizational information

questionText: "Coercive power" is based on:
options: The power holder's access to information and knowledge that others need
The respect and admiration others have for the power holder's personal qualities
The ability to threaten or apply punishment to influence others' behaviour
The formal authority assigned to a position in the organizational hierarchy

questionText: "Expert power" derives from:
options: The formal authority granted by the organizational hierarchy
The ability to reward compliant behaviour with valued outcomes
The possession of special knowledge, skills, or expertise that others value and need
The personal attractiveness and charisma of the power holder

questionText: "Referent power" in organizational behaviour is based on:
options: The formal authority associated with a managerial position
The ability to administer punishments and withhold valued rewards
Identification with and admiration for the power holder's personal qualities and characteristics
Access to critical organizational information that others do not have

questionText: Which of the following types of power is MOST closely associated with transformational leadership?
options: Legitimate power
Coercive power
Reward power
Referent power

questionText: "Organizational politics" in OB refers to:
options: The formal process by which organizational policies and rules are developed
Activities that are not required as part of one's formal role but that influence the distribution of advantages and disadvantages in the organization
The process of negotiating employment contracts and collective bargaining agreements
The formal decision-making procedures established by the organization's governance structure

questionText: Which of the following is an example of "political behaviour" in an organization?
options: A manager submitting a formal performance appraisal for a direct report
An employee forming alliances with influential colleagues to gain support for a project proposal
A department head allocating the annual budget according to established organizational procedures
A supervisor conducting a disciplinary meeting with an underperforming employee

questionText: Which of the following factors MOST contributes to political behaviour in organizations?
options: Clear, objective performance measurement systems and transparent decision-making processes
Ambiguity in roles and performance criteria, scarce resources, and high-stakes decisions
Strong organizational cultures with well-established norms and values
Highly centralized decision-making with little discretion at lower organizational levels

questionText: "Impression management" in organizational behaviour refers to:
options: The formal performance evaluation process conducted by management
The process by which individuals attempt to control the impression others form of them
The management of organizational reputation through public relations activities
The process of designing and maintaining the physical appearance of the workplace

questionText: Which of the following is a LEGITIMATE political behaviour in organizations?
options: Spreading false information about a colleague to undermine their reputation
Withholding critical information from a competitor within the organization
Building a broad base of support by networking, developing coalitions, and demonstrating competence
Claiming credit for a colleague's achievements to gain favor with senior management

questionText: "Dependency" is a key concept in understanding power. According to this concept, power increases when:
options: Resources become widely available and easily substitutable
The power holder controls resources that are scarce, important, and non-substitutable
The power holder reduces their control over organizational resources
Decision-making authority is equally distributed across all organizational members

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the relationship between power and leadership in organizations?
options: Power and leadership are identical concepts that always occur together
Effective leadership requires the use of coercive power to ensure compliance
Leadership involves influencing others toward goals, and power is the resource that makes this influence possible
Leaders rely exclusively on legitimate authority and never use informal power sources

questionText: A warehouse supervisor always meets the team in the morning, greets each worker by name, and acknowledges good performance publicly. According to OB, this behaviour is MOST likely to influence which of the following?
options: The formal organizational structure and reporting relationships
Employee job satisfaction, motivation, and organizational commitment
The organization's financial performance and budget allocation
The design of the warehouse layout and material handling systems

questionText: A supply chain analyst consistently attributes delivery failures to external factors such as traffic or supplier delays, while crediting personal skill for successful deliveries. This pattern BEST illustrates which perceptual bias?
options: The halo effect
Stereotyping
The fundamental attribution error
Self-serving bias

questionText: A logistics manager wants to reduce absenteeism among warehouse staff. Applying operant conditioning, which of the following approaches is MOST likely to be effective?
options: Explaining the organizational policy on absenteeism in the employee handbook
Implementing a reward system that recognizes employees with perfect attendance records
Increasing base salaries for all warehouse employees
Reorganizing the warehouse layout to improve physical working conditions

questionText: A newly formed procurement team is experiencing significant disagreements about roles and decision-making authority. According to Tuckman's model, this team is MOST likely in which stage of development?
options: Forming
Storming
Norming
Performing

questionText: A logistics team has been working together for two years and performs at a consistently high level. Members trust each other, communicate openly, and resolve conflicts constructively. According to Tuckman's model, this team is MOST likely in which stage?
options: Forming
Storming
Norming
Performing

questionText: A supply chain manager who consistently delivers on promises, treats all team members fairly, and demonstrates technical expertise is building which types of power MOST effectively?
options: Legitimate and coercive power
Expert and referent power
Reward and coercive power
Legitimate and reward power

questionText: An experienced logistics coordinator believes she has no control over her career outcomes and that promotions are determined by luck and favoritism. This belief BEST reflects which personality characteristic?
options: High internal locus of control
High self-efficacy
High conscientiousness
External locus of control

questionText: A freight forwarding manager wants to motivate a high-achieving employee who values personal growth and challenge. Applying McClelland's theory, which approach is MOST appropriate?
options: Assigning the employee to a stable, routine role with predictable outcomes
Increasing the employee's base salary and annual bonus
Assigning the employee to a challenging, high-visibility project with clear accountability for results
Organizing social events to strengthen the employee's relationships with colleagues

questionText: A procurement team's performance has declined despite receiving pay raises. Applying Herzberg's two-factor theory, which conclusion is MOST justified?
options: The team needs additional hygiene factor improvements to become motivated
Salary is a motivator and should be increased further to restore performance
The pay raises only addressed hygiene factors; motivators such as recognition and meaningful work must also be addressed
The team's performance decline is unrelated to motivation and requires structural reorganization

questionText: Two departments in a logistics company — operations and procurement — are in conflict over resource allocation. To resolve this, the CEO introduces a company-wide efficiency drive that requires both departments to collaborate. This approach BEST reflects:
options: Competing strategy for conflict resolution
Avoidance of intergroup conflict
Introduction of a superordinate goal to reduce intergroup conflict
Accommodation strategy where one group surrenders to the other

questionText: A transport manager sets a specific target of reducing fuel costs by 15% within six months and provides weekly performance feedback to the team. This approach is MOST consistent with which motivational theory?
options: Maslow's hierarchy of needs
Herzberg's two-factor theory
Locke and Latham's goal-setting theory
Adams' equity theory

questionText: An employee who learns to complete customs documentation accurately by watching a more experienced colleague and then practicing the process independently is BEST demonstrating which type of learning?
options: Classical conditioning
Operant conditioning
Social learning
Fixed-ratio reinforcement

questionText: A logistics company promotes a junior analyst to team leader based on technical excellence. However, the analyst struggles to manage the team. This situation MOST likely reflects:
options: A failure of the operant conditioning learning process
The halo effect — assuming technical excellence predicts managerial effectiveness
Inadequate reward power in the new leadership role
A groupthink problem in the promotion decision process

questionText: Which of the following BEST illustrates "organizational commitment" among logistics employees?
options: Employees who comply with organizational rules only to avoid disciplinary action
Employees who identify strongly with the organization's mission, stay during difficult periods, and go beyond their formal job requirements
Employees who remain with the organization only because switching jobs is inconvenient
Employees who perform well only when directly supervised by their manager

questionText: A supply chain manager notices that a team member reduces effort when working in groups but performs well individually. This MOST likely reflects:
options: Role ambiguity causing the employee to be unclear about expectations
Groupthink suppressing individual initiative in team settings
Social loafing due to diffused responsibility in the group context
Group polarization causing the employee to adopt more extreme positions

questionText: According to equity theory, which of the following employees is MOST at risk of reducing their work effort?
options: An employee who perceives their rewards are perfectly proportional to their contributions
An employee who perceives they are receiving more than colleagues doing equivalent work
An employee who perceives they are contributing more than colleagues but receiving equivalent or lower rewards
An employee who recently received a promotion and a significant pay increase

questionText: A logistics director uses data and logical reasoning to persuade the board to invest in a new warehouse management system. This approach to influence MOST reflects the use of which type of power?
options: Coercive power
Referent power
Legitimate power
Expert power

questionText: An employee behaves differently when interacting with customers compared to when working with colleagues, consciously adjusting their communication style and professional image. This BEST illustrates:
options: Role conflict causing inconsistent behaviour across different contexts
Impression management — consciously controlling the image projected to different audiences
Cognitive dissonance — holding contradictory attitudes about the work role
The fundamental attribution error — misjudging others' intentions in different settings

questionText: A procurement manager discovers that two team members hold opposing attitudes about a new supplier evaluation policy and are avoiding each other. Which OB concept BEST explains the root cause if both employees privately agree the policy is good but publicly criticize it to maintain group acceptance?
options: Social loafing
Groupthink and conformity pressure
Role ambiguity
Group polarization

questionText: A warehouse team that has high cohesiveness but maintains low performance norms will MOST likely demonstrate which outcome?
options: High individual performance driven by strong interpersonal relationships
High productivity due to the motivating effect of social bonds
Consistently low productivity as the group enforces restrictive output norms
High levels of innovation and creative problem-solving

questionText: Which of the following BEST explains why understanding perception is important for logistics managers?
options: Perception determines the physical layout of the workplace and workflow design
Managers' perceptions of employee performance and potential directly influence decisions about promotions, assignments, and development
Perception is relevant only in customer-facing roles and has no bearing on internal management decisions
Perceptual accuracy is determined entirely by the manager's level of education and formal training

questionText: A supply chain company introduces a mentoring program where experienced employees guide new recruits. This program MOST directly leverages which learning mechanism?
options: Operant conditioning through reward and punishment
Classical conditioning through stimulus-response pairing
Social learning through observation and modelling
Fixed-interval reinforcement to shape behaviour systematically

questionText: A logistics manager who has referent power but no formal authority succeeds in influencing colleagues in other departments to cooperate on a cross-functional project. This situation BEST illustrates which OB concept?
options: Legitimate authority as the basis of organizational influence
The ability to exercise influence without formal authority through personal power
The use of coercive power to compel compliance from reluctant colleagues
Organizational politics through self-serving manipulation of colleagues

questionText: Which of the following is the MOST likely consequence of unresolved "role conflict" among supply chain managers?
options: Increased clarity about job expectations and performance standards
Higher levels of job satisfaction and organizational commitment
Increased stress, reduced job satisfaction, and potential decline in performance
Stronger group cohesiveness and improved inter-departmental coordination

questionText: A team of logistics professionals is making a critical procurement decision. Initially, most members slightly favour a particular supplier. After group discussion, the team selects that supplier with much greater conviction and dismisses all concerns about risk. This BEST illustrates:
options: Social loafing causing disengagement from the decision-making process
Group polarization amplifying the initial preference during discussion
Groupthink suppressing individual dissent to maintain harmony
The fundamental attribution error distorting the team's risk assessment

questionText: "Work ethic" in organizational behaviour is BEST described as:
options: The set of technical skills required to perform a job at an acceptable standard
A set of values based on the moral virtues of hard work, diligence, responsibility, and commitment to doing one's job well
The formal code of conduct documented in the organization's employee handbook
The level of financial compensation an employee believes they deserve for their work

questionText: Which of the following behaviours BEST demonstrates a strong work ethic in a logistics environment?
options: Completing only the minimum required tasks and leaving promptly at the end of the shift
Taking personal responsibility for delivery errors and proactively identifying and communicating solutions
Delegating all challenging tasks to colleagues to avoid the risk of failure
Prioritizing personal comfort and convenience over team and organizational needs

questionText: "Professional ethics" in the context of supply chain management involves:
options: Maximizing personal financial gain through all available means
Adhering to accepted standards of conduct, fairness, transparency, and integrity in all professional dealings
Complying with organizational rules only when directly observed by a supervisor
Prioritizing speed and cost efficiency above all other professional considerations

questionText: An employee who consistently arrives on time, meets deadlines, communicates proactively about challenges, and maintains high quality standards is demonstrating which of the following OB concepts?
options: High neuroticism and low agreeableness
External locus of control and low self-efficacy
Conscientiousness and strong organizational commitment
High need for affiliation and low need for achievement

questionText: Which of the following BEST illustrates the application of work ethic in procurement management?
options: Selecting suppliers based on personal relationships rather than objective evaluation criteria
Accepting gifts from suppliers in exchange for preferential treatment in the bidding process
Conducting fair, transparent, and rigorous supplier evaluations based on established criteria
Approving procurement decisions without proper documentation to save time

questionText: A customs clearing officer who consistently follows established procedures, maintains accurate documentation, and refuses bribes regardless of external pressure is demonstrating which professional quality?
options: Social loafing and lack of initiative
Referent power based on personal charisma
Professional integrity and strong work ethic
External locus of control and low self-efficacy

questionText: Which of the following is the PRIMARY reason why work ethic and professional conduct are emphasized as competencies in the Logistics and Supply Chain Management program?
options: Logistics professionals work in low-risk environments where ethical lapses have minimal consequences
Professional integrity and ethical conduct are foundational to building trust with clients, suppliers, and regulatory authorities in logistics operations
Ethical conduct is enforced exclusively by regulatory agencies and requires no personal commitment from professionals
Work ethic is relevant only for senior managers and not for operational staff

questionText: Which of the following behaviours represents a violation of professional ethics in supply chain management?
options: Disclosing a conflict of interest to management before participating in a supplier selection process
Sharing confidential supplier pricing information with a competing supplier
Reporting suspected procurement fraud through the organization's formal reporting channels
Refusing to approve a purchase order that does not comply with organizational procurement policy

questionText: "Organizational citizenship behaviour" (OCB) refers to:
options: Behaviours that employees are explicitly required to perform as part of their formal job description
Discretionary behaviours that go beyond formal job requirements and contribute positively to the organization
Behaviours regulated by the organization's formal code of conduct and disciplinary policy
Behaviours required by law as conditions of employment in regulated industries

questionText: Which of the following is an example of "organizational citizenship behaviour" in a logistics firm?
options: Completing assigned delivery routes within the required time window
Voluntarily assisting a new colleague to learn the warehouse management system after hours
Submitting a formal complaint about a workplace policy through the grievance procedure
Requesting overtime pay for additional hours worked beyond the standard shift

questionText: Which of the following BEST explains why OB is relevant to logistics and supply chain managers?
options: OB provides the technical knowledge needed to operate warehouse management systems
Understanding individual and group behaviour enables logistics managers to build motivated, high-performing teams that deliver superior supply chain outcomes
OB is primarily a theoretical academic discipline with limited application in operational settings
OB is only relevant for human resources professionals and has no bearing on logistics management

questionText: A logistics company wants to build a culture of continuous improvement. Which combination of OB concepts would MOST effectively support this goal?
options: High coercive power, strict rule enforcement, and autocratic leadership
Strong work ethic, intrinsic motivation, positive reinforcement of improvement behaviours, and psychological safety in teams
High levels of social loafing, groupthink, and conformity to established norms
External locus of control, low self-efficacy, and avoidance of challenging tasks

questionText: A procurement manager is assigned to lead a cross-functional team for the first time. To build trust and influence without formal authority, which approach is MOST aligned with OB principles?
options: Relying exclusively on legitimate power derived from the formal managerial title
Using coercive power to ensure compliance from team members
Demonstrating expertise, treating all members fairly, communicating openly, and building referent power through integrity and competence
Avoiding conflict at all costs by accommodating all team members' preferences

questionText: An organization's logistics division is experiencing high turnover among experienced staff. Applying OB frameworks, which of the following is the MOST comprehensive diagnostic approach?
options: Immediately increasing salaries for all logistics staff to prevent further departures
Examining job satisfaction, organizational commitment, motivation factors, leadership quality, work group dynamics, and the organizational culture to identify root causes
Replacing all departing employees with new hires and focusing exclusively on onboarding efficiency
Reducing job demands to decrease stress and prevent further attrition

questionText: Which of the following BEST summarizes the contribution of organizational behaviour to effective supply chain management?
options: OB provides the mathematical and quantitative tools needed to optimize supply chain operations
OB provides insights into how individual, group, and organizational factors shape the human systems that make supply chains function effectively or ineffectively
OB is irrelevant to supply chain management since supply chains are technical systems driven by data and technology
OB contributes only to the HR function of supply chain organizations, not to operational or strategic management

questionText: A transport company's management team wants to improve team performance across its depot locations. Based on OB research, which of the following interventions is MOST likely to be effective?
options: Standardizing all job roles to eliminate individual discretion and variability
Increasing surveillance and monitoring of all employee activities
Building clear team goals, fostering cohesion, ensuring role clarity, providing feedback, and recognizing performance
Eliminating all informal communication channels to prevent social loafing

questionText: Which of the following scenarios BEST illustrates the application of the "Big Five" personality model in a logistics recruitment context?
options: Selecting warehouse supervisors based exclusively on their technical knowledge of inventory systems
Using personality assessments to identify candidates high in conscientiousness and emotional stability for high-responsibility logistics roles
Recruiting candidates based solely on their educational qualifications and years of experience
Selecting candidates based on the halo effect created by impressive physical appearance and confident body language

questionText: A supply chain manager who always acknowledges uncertainty, seeks input from the team before making decisions, and openly admits mistakes is demonstrating which combination of OB qualities?
options: High coercive power and autocratic leadership style
External locus of control and low self-efficacy
Intellectual humility, psychological safety promotion, and authentic leadership
Social loafing and avoidance of personal accountability

questionText: Which of the following BEST explains why diversity in work groups can enhance organizational performance?
options: Diverse groups always experience less conflict than homogeneous groups
Diverse groups bring a broader range of perspectives, experiences, and ideas that can improve problem-solving and decision quality
Diversity reduces the need for formal coordination mechanisms within groups
Homogeneous groups consistently outperform diverse groups on routine operational tasks

questionText: A logistics firm's senior management observes that front-line employees consistently go beyond their formal job requirements — helping colleagues, suggesting process improvements, and representing the company positively to customers. This MOST likely reflects:
options: Social loafing being masked by surface-level compliance with organizational rules
Employees acting to avoid coercive punishment from their supervisors
A strong organizational culture that fosters high organizational citizenship behaviour and intrinsic motivation
The application of external locus of control beliefs in the workplace

questionText: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between "attitudes" and "behaviour" in organizational behaviour research?
options: Attitudes always perfectly predict behaviour with no exceptions
Attitudes and behaviour are completely unrelated and should be studied separately
Attitudes generally predict behaviour, but the relationship is influenced by situational constraints, attitude strength, and the specificity of the attitude
Behaviour always determines attitudes, and attitudes never influence behaviour

questionText: A procurement team completes a major supplier negotiation successfully ahead of schedule. The team leader publicly praises each member's contribution in the next department meeting. According to OB principles, this action MOST directly reinforces:
options: Coercive power through the threat of public humiliation for poor performance
Positive reinforcement of desirable behaviour, strengthening the likelihood of similar performance in future
The fundamental attribution error by attributing success to individual effort alone
Groupthink by discouraging any future dissent from team members

questionText: Which of the following OB concepts MOST directly explains why two employees in identical job roles with identical salaries can have very different levels of job satisfaction?
options: The formal authority structure determines job satisfaction equally for all employees in the same role
Individual differences in personality, values, expectations, and perception mean that the same objective conditions are experienced differently
Job satisfaction is determined exclusively by salary level and has no relationship to other individual or contextual factors
Job satisfaction is a fixed personality trait that does not change regardless of the work environment

questionText: A logistics company implements a new shift rotation system. Some employees embrace the change enthusiastically while others resist it strongly. Applying OB, which of the following BEST explains this difference?
options: The employees who resist have lower intelligence and cannot adapt to new systems
Individual differences in personality, values, locus of control, and past experiences with change shape how each employee perceives and responds to the new system
Resistance to change is always motivated by laziness and unwillingness to work
Employees who embrace change are always motivated by financial incentives while resisters are not

questionText: Which of the following BEST summarizes the role of a logistics manager who applies OB principles effectively?
options: A manager who focuses exclusively on technical process efficiency and ignores the human dimensions of the work environment
A manager who uses coercive power to enforce compliance and eliminate all forms of individual discretion

A manager who understands and leverages individual motivation, builds cohesive and high-performing teams, manages power and politics ethically, and fosters a culture of integrity and continuous improvement
A manager who applies a single fixed management style consistently to all employees regardless of their individual characteristics and needs
